title: Sonic the Hedgehog
wiki_lead:
Sonic the Hedgehog is a video game series and media franchise created by the Japanese developers Yuji Naka, Naoto Ohshima, and Hirokazu Yasuhara for Sega. The franchise follows Sonic, an anthropomorphic blue hedgehog with supersonic speed, who battles the mad scientist Doctor Eggman and his robot army. The main Sonic the Hedgehog games are platformers mostly developed by Sonic Team; other games, developed by various studios, include spin-offs in the racing, fighting, party, and sports genres. The franchise also incorporates printed media, animations, films, and merchandise.
Naka, Ohshima, and Yasuhara developed the first Sonic game, released in 1991 for the Sega Genesis, to provide Sega with a mascot to compete with Nintendo's Mario. Its success helped Sega become one of the leading video game companies during the fourth generation of video game consoles in the early 1990s. Sega Technical Institute developed the next three main Sonic game. After a hiatus during the unsuccessful Saturn era, the first major 3D Sonic game, Sonic Adventure, was released in 1998 for the Dreamcast. Sega exited the console market and shifted to third-party development in 2001, continuing the series on Nintendo, Xbox, and PlayStation systems. Takashi Iizuka has been the series' producer since 2010.
Sonic's recurring elements include a ring-based health system, level locales such as Green Hill Zone, and fast-paced gameplay. The games typically feature Sonic setting out to stop Eggman's schemes for world domination, and the player navigates levels that include springs, slopes, bottomless pits, and vertical loops. Later games added a large cast of characters; some, such as Tails, Knuckles the Echidna, and Shadow the Hedgehog, have starred in spin-offs. The franchise has crossed over with other series' including rival platformer Mario, in Mario & Sonic.
Sonic the Hedgehog is Sega's flagship franchise, one of the bestselling video game franchises, and one of the highest-grossing media franchises. Series sales and free-to-play mobile game downloads totaled 1.77 billion as of 2024. The Genesis Sonic games have been described as representative of the culture of the 1990s and listed among the greatest of all time. Although later games, such as the 2006 game, received poorer reviews, Sonic is influential in the video game industry and is frequently referenced in popular culture. The franchise is known for its fandom that produces unofficial media, such as fan art and fan games.

History


1990–1991: Conception and first game

By 1990, the Japanese video game company Sega wanted a foothold in the video game console market with its 16-bit console, the Sega Genesis. Sega's efforts had been stymied by the dominance of Nintendo; the Genesis did not have a large install base and Nintendo did not take Sega seriously as a competitor. grok_lead: Sonic the Hedgehog is a long-running Japanese video game franchise created and owned by Sega, featuring the titular protagonist, a blue anthropomorphic hedgehog renowned for his supersonic speed and adventurous spirit as he battles the mad scientist Dr. Ivo "Eggman" Robotnik to thwart world domination schemes. The series debuted with the 1991 platformer Sonic the Hedgehog for the Sega Genesis, developed by a team including designer Naoto Ohshima, game designer Hirokazu Yasuhara, and programmer Yuji Naka, who aimed to craft a cool, fast-paced mascot to rival Nintendo's Mario during the 16-bit console wars. Inspired by American pop culture, environmental themes, and the hedgehog's ability to curl into a spiky ball for attacks, Sonic's design emphasized simplicity and attitude, with his blue color matching Sega's logo. The franchise has spanned over 30 years, encompassing more than 70 video games across platforms from the Sega Genesis to modern consoles like the Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 5, blending 2D side-scrolling platforming with 3D open-world adventures in titles such as Sonic Adventure (1998), Sonic Heroes (2003), Sonic Generations (2011), Sonic Mania (2017), Sonic Frontiers (2022), and Sonic X Shadow Generations (2024). Core gameplay revolves around high-speed running, ring collection for protection, spin dash attacks, and collecting Chaos Emeralds to transform into Super Sonic for boss battles against Robotnik's mechanical minions. Supporting characters like the two-tailed fox Miles "Tails" Prower, the echidna Knuckles the Echidna, and the anti-hero Shadow the Hedgehog have joined the ensemble, enabling team-based mechanics in later entries. As of 2022, the video game series has achieved lifetime sales and downloads exceeding 1.5 billion units worldwide, making it one of Sega's flagship properties and a cornerstone of gaming history. The filmsâ Sonic the Hedgehog (2020), Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (2022), Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (2024), and the upcoming Sonic the Hedgehog 4 (2027)âhave collectively grossed over $1 billion at the global box office, with the third installment alone surpassing $492 million. This cross-media success, bolstered by merchandise, theme park attractions, and collaborations like the McLaren Racing partnership, underscores Sonic's enduring cultural impact as a symbol of speed, freedom, and Sega 's innovative legacy.
